objective: Coordinator's go-ahead (18 November 2026) on FIRST-KNOT-20261118-001's direction 3: the fewest counts on every small arrangement of touching knots (up to five parity knots of three to five places, each shared distinction in two knots, counted up to renaming), asking which dimensions are typical and which rare (the owner's no-choice direction: nothing chooses an arrangement). Frozen rule: the dimension is the largest set of chains of offshoots born together with one common partner. Stop at a rule that predicts every dimension, or a counterexample. Serves G2, G17 and G1.
status: Complete 2026-11-18 (Successful; referee pending; 2 of 265 shards pending): over 26,241 distinct arrangements of up to five touching parity knots of three to five places, the cheapest growth stalls at once in 41.6%, closes in 14.1%, grows one-dimensionally in 7.9% and two-dimensionally in 36.2%; three- and four-dimensional growth is rare (0.16%), and seven rings of five knots grow faster than any power; dimensions count junctions by round. Two-dimensional is typical, not forced. The chain rule (largest class of chains born together) held in 98.7% of growing arrangements, every exception being one more; 3 of 8 frozen predictions held.
stop_rule: Proof, one frozen census, referee hand-off, report.
title: Which dimensions does the cheapest growth give across arrangements of touching knots?
